clauses.reason: The operative paragraph reads "I hereby further exempt the said Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending August 31, 1939." The exemption is a one-time permission for a fixed period and the period is stated in the order itself. By its own terms it runs through August 31, 1939, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading ends it when August 31, 1939 begins. State on 2026-10-14: terminated, the permission having been exhausted by lapse of the stated period. Executive Order No. 8231, signed August 31, 1939, is a later event and not an end: its operative sentence reads "I hereby further exempt the said Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending February 29, 1940." It grants Edward M. Weeks a further exemption for six months ending February 29, 1940; it does not revoke or shorten this order, and under the owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md an extension is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7945 of August 4, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending August 31, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The recital identifies Edward M. Weeks as a person who had been exempted for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 7413 of July 10, 1936, and No. 7635 of June 16, 1937; that earlier exemption is a separate instrument, and nothing in it affects when this one ends. The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362909, Common Crawl capture 2025-11-11T15:13:09Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7945, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on August 31, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The packet records later extension order(s) No. 8231 (August 31, 1939); each is entered as a later event, and the machine search hits for this order (OFR catalog and held-text name search) are exactly those order(s).

savings.reason: The order grants a permission for a fixed period and contains no saving or transfer provision. What it left behind, Edward M. Weeks's continued federal employment during the period, accrued while the period ran; no duty or right continues after August 31, 1939 by the order's own terms. Any exemption after August 31, 1939 rests on the separate later order(s) recorded as later events.
